title: Constant coefficients on the pro-etale site
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete ring (not necessarily commutative) and let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ be the sheaf of rings of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $u^{-1}$ for inverse image of sheaves of rings, left adjoint to the direct image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $a\in\Lambda$ write $\eta_T(a)$ for the section obtained from the constant function $a$ by the sheafification defining $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$. Define $\rho:\Lambda_{V,\Proet}\to u_*\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$ by sending each constant section $a$ on an object $W\to V$ to $\eta_U(a)$ restricted to $W\times_VU$; on an element of the defining presheaf use these sections on its open fibres and glue, then extend uniquely by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $c_u:u^{-1}\Lambda_{V,\Proet}\to\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$ be the ring-sheaf morphism adjoint to $\rho$. Then $c_u$ is an isomorphism. For commutative $\Lambda$, under the unique identifications with constant sheaves preserving constant sections, this is exactly the structure map $c^u_\Lambda$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Here inverse image and the coefficient objects are sheaves, with the indicated sheafifications; in particular for $U=\varnothing$ both sides are the zero ring sheaf and $c_u$ is its unique isomorphism.

proof.text: Naturality of the fibre-product function map follows from pullback.lift_fst on underlying scheme points, passage to connected components and naturality of toSheafify. This proves finiteCoefficientDirectImageApp_naturality for the recorded base-change functor.

The already stated finiteCoefficientScalarMap_locallyBijective of def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules supplies the open-fibre argument. The constant-presheaf sheafification unit is locally bijective. Its composite with finiteCoefficientConstantComparison is exactly finiteCoefficientScalarMap by the sheafification adjunction. Cancel local bijectivity of the unit, then apply Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso. Uniqueness among constant-preserving comparisons is sheafify_hom_ext.

For arbitrary ring coefficients, prove the comparison square between finiteCoefficientInverseImageMap and proEtaleConstantInverseImageMap. Naturality of the inverse-image adjunction reduces it to a direct-image equality. Precompose with the constant-presheaf sheafification unit and use the defining equations of both sheafification extensions. Both maps then send each scalar to the same constant function on the fibre product, so the equality is pointwise reflexivity. The stated commutative comparison is a specialization of this ring-valued square.

Base change preserves the terminal pro-etale object. Compose the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction on V with the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction and the sectionwise direct-image evaluation isomorphism. This composite and the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction on U have the same right adjoint. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives an isomorphism; evaluating the Hom equivalences proves that its component is exactly proEtaleConstantInverseImageMap. The comparison square and the invertible finiteCoefficientConstantComparison maps imply that finiteCoefficientInverseImageMap is invertible, by cancellation of an isomorphism. This argument works in RingCat without commutativity.

When U is empty, every pro-etale object W over U has empty underlying scheme. The empty sieve covers W (ProEt.bot_mem_topology), so a ring sheaf has terminal sections there (isTerminalSectionsOfIsEmpty). The forgetful functor from rings to types preserves this terminal object, giving a singleton section type. Apply this to both coefficient sheaves, then use sectionwise extensionality to prove uniqueness of their morphism.

proof_origin.place: Blueprint order 1235, Stacks Tags 04B3, 0H7J and 09A5; G1 Lean proof using the stated locally bijective scalar map and uniqueness of left adjoints. The generic constant-ring adjunction calculation follows the existing private proEtaleConstantComparison_isIso proof in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.ProfiniteCoefficientInverseImage, generalized from CommRingCat to RingCat.
